name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behaviour
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social platforms, from the CooRnet/CLSB methodology to the ongoing VERA-AI Alert monitoring system. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains the most active line of current output.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation Narratives
description: Study of disinformation, misinformation and 'fake news' as phenomena within the hybrid media system, including narrative monitoring around crises such as COVID-19, the war in Ukraine, and elections. Forms the conceptual umbrella connecting MINE and EU-funded projects like PROMPT and vera.ai.

name: Platform Governance & Researcher Data Access
description: Research and advocacy on social media APIs, data-access regimes and platform policy under the EU Digital Services Act, including work as a DSA/ECAT expert, analyses of Meta's political content reduction policy, and the fallout from CrowdTangle's shutdown for research infrastructure.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Influence Operations
description: Emerging work on how generative AI is used in coordinated deceptive campaigns, including AI-generated visual persuasion in gambling promotion and 'zombie internet' information operations, reflecting the researcher's pivot toward AI-era manipulation tactics.

name: LLMs & Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological research on integrating large language models into content classification, annotation and clustering pipelines for political discourse and news analysis, addressing validation, reliability and human-machine disagreement in social science workflows.

name: Elections & Social Media Political Communication
description: Empirical mapping of political news coverage, partisan attention, advertising and citizen engagement around specific elections — Italy (2018, 2022), Germany (2021), Brazil (post-Bolsonaro) — a recurring empirical anchor of the MINE programme.

name: Political Polarization & Partisan Media Ecosystems
description: Analysis of insularity, cross-partisan interaction, affective engagement and polarization dynamics across Facebook communities and traditional/social media interplay, a persistent theoretical concern linking older and current publications.

name: Problematic Health Information Online
description: Research on the circulation of low-quality and coordinated health-related content on social media, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration and cross-country studies in India and Nigeria funded by the Gates Foundation.

name: Social TV & Second-Screen Audience Engagement
description: Earlier but recurring strand studying Twitter/second-screen participation around television broadcasts and talk shows, foundational to the researcher's move into large-scale social media data analysis.

name: Digital Methods for Computational Social Science
description: Methodological reflections and tools for using social media as a research data source, including survey recruitment via Facebook ads, ethics of computational social science, and embedding/clustering techniques — the toolkit underlying all substantive MINE research.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.
